title: Playback surface contract — one fault table and one ordered-event reducer every client reproduces

kinds.none: Nothing is drawn over the picture.
kinds.indicator: In-chrome progress indicator; the picture is presenting behind it.
kinds.banner: A notice strip with the fault's actions; the picture is untouched.
kinds.blocking: The picture is covered. Only ever drawn over a player its recovery owner has already stopped, or over a picture that is not presenting.

input_failed_state.note: The player input contract's `failed` state is a BLOCKING surface whose class is a prompt or a terminal — a fault with actions the viewer must answer. A full-screen `preparing`/`buffering`/`recovering` is blocking pixels, not routing: it keeps today's routing, per PLAYBACK-SURFACE-CONTRACT.md §4.

notes: refused_progress_ms is CONTINUOUS presenting on the attached generation, not accumulated playback.
buffering_min_ms debounces the surface, not the fault: a `media_waiting` fault exists from the moment it is raised and is simply not drawn until it has lasted this long.

A hidden page freezes every timer as well as every evidence sample. The reducer does this by carrying the hidden interval forward: on becoming visible again every fault's raise time is shifted by however long the page was hidden, and the continuous-presenting clock is reset, because no sample bridged the gap.

disagreement_notice_ms retires the "Playback recovered" banner a demotion leaves behind (§3.2). Its actions stay valid while the picture could still fail again; this much CONTINUOUS presenting is the point at which the offer is stale. Ruled by the implementer 2026-09-13 in Paul's absence — §3.1 says such a banner does not expire "while an action is still valid" and does not say when that ends; a banner with no end is the Android `playFailure` defect wearing a different hat.

presenting_after_raise is the contract's "presenting evidence on the NEW attached generation": what makes the evidence count is that the run of presentation BEGAN at or after the fault was raised. An owner that reopens in place, on the same generation, produces exactly that, and a recovering indicator that only a new generation could retire would outlive every in-place recovery.

errors.blocking_without_stop: A source whose CLASS is blocking was raised with player_stopped false. The reducer logs the error and leaves the surface unchanged; it never renders the fault. Every source mapping to a blocking class carries `requires.player_stopped` so the table and the reducer cannot disagree.
errors.source_context_mismatch: A source was raised in a context no row for that id declares.
errors.unknown_source: A source id that is in no row was raised.

identity_notes: A fault about the ATTACHED media carries `attached` and no `intent`; it is retired by that media's presentation evidence.

A fault about a PENDING DESTINATION carries an `intent`. Evidence never retires it, with one exception the class table states outright: `refused` also retires on `refused_progress_ms` of continuous presentation, because a viewer whose picture has been fine for that long has been told.

A fault whose `attached` generation is retired stops being about anything and is dropped (`surface_cleared {by: attached_retired}`). That is identity, not one of the class's `retired_by` rules, so it applies to blocking faults too — otherwise a `stopped` prompt would outlive the attempt it described and sit over the next one.

Each retirement reason is a property of the CLASS, not of the event: `intent_settled` retires only classes whose `retired_by` names it, so a prompt the viewer has to answer is not swept away by a seek landing underneath it. `attached_retired` is the one exception, and the note above says why.

`owner_success: G` is the recovery owner reporting that its recovery produced attached generation G. There is one recovery owner per player, so it retires every `recovering` fault, not only the ones about the generation it replaced.

cases.name: canplay_is_inert
cases.note: A platform event never moves the surface. Only the client's own presentation proof does.

cases.name: web_safari_boundary_waiting
cases.note: A wait shorter than buffering_min_ms draws nothing; the flash is the defect.

cases.name: web_fatal_over_live_buffer
cases.note: The defect, exactly: an hls.js fatal with 30 s of buffer still playing. While the ladder has a rung left it is progress over a moving picture — an indicator, never a full screen — and the owner's stop is what makes it terminal.

cases.name: android_watchdog_restart_under_stop
cases.note: playWhenReady=false before the raise means no evidence arrives; the prompt stands until the viewer answers it.

cases.name: apple_readiness_rungs_left_is_recovering
cases.note: A readiness deadline that still has a rung to try is progress, never a prompt.

cases.name: web_failed_change_sticky
cases.note: A change that failed is a banner over a predecessor that never stopped playing.

cases.name: terminal_wording_transport_exception
cases.note: D1: the control-plane terminal verdict arms wording; a transport-class failure keeps the client's own sentence.

events.title: Playback stopped.
events.detail: The connection to the server was lost.

expect.title: Playback stopped.
expect.detail: The connection to the server was lost.

cases.name: blocking_raised_over_a_presenting_picture
cases.note: The disagreement is decided when the fault is raised, not whenever the next evidence sample happens to land.

cases.name: disagreement_banner_retires_after_continuous_progress
cases.note: A recovered banner that never ends is the Android playFailure defect wearing a different hat.

cases.name: exhausted_survives_intent_settled
cases.note: A prompt the viewer has to answer is not swept away because a seek landed underneath it.

cases.name: promotion_only_by_the_owner_stop
cases.note: A decoder failure over a live 410 is its own fault with its own sentence. Folding it into the 410 is the misattribution the ledger exists to prevent.

cases.name: promotion_keeps_the_class_default_actions
cases.note: A terminal full screen with no Try again and no Close is one the viewer cannot leave.

cases.name: recovering_retired_by_presenting_after_in_place_reopen
cases.note: The owner that reopens on the same element reports no new generation. An indicator only a new generation could retire outlives every in-place recovery.

cases.name: refused_continuity_interrupted
cases.note: Continuous means continuous: a break in presentation restarts the clock.

cases.name: stale_generation_evidence_is_ignored
cases.note: A predecessor moving does not forgive a replacement that failed — the review's second blocker, in one sequence. The sample is not evidence AT ALL: it may not promote a full screen to an indicator, and it may not resolve a disagreement.

cases.name: hold_timer_frozen_while_hidden
cases.note: A 30 s hold the viewer backgrounded for half a minute has not been on screen for 30 s.

cases.name: refused_progress_clock_frozen_while_hidden
cases.note: A failed change is not forgiven by presentation the page could not observe.

cases.name: promotion_needs_the_same_generation
cases.note: The owner stopping a pending successor does not turn the incumbent's 410 into a terminal.

cases.name: refused_continuity_needs_a_presenting_picture
cases.note: A paused picture accumulates no continuous progress, however long it stays paused.

precedence_note: Rows are scanned in order and the first row whose id and context both match wins. The highest-severity drawable fault owns the surface; faults of equal severity are broken by recency, newest first.
